name: Multimessenger observation of blazar TXS 0506+056 with IceCube-170922A
notes: The paper is authored jointly by IceCube and the Fermi-LAT, MAGIC, AGILE, ASAS-SN, HAWC, H.E.S.S., INTEGRAL, Kanata, Kiso, Kapteyn, Liverpool, Subaru, Swift/NuSTAR, VERITAS and VLA teams; only collaboration:icecube exists in the atlas so far.

significance.note: The abstract states no significance. The companion paper (arXiv:1807.08794) reports 3.5σ evidence for an earlier neutrino flare from the same direction.
significance.quote: This observation of a neutrino in spatial coincidence with a gamma-ray emitting blazar during an active phase suggests that blazars may be a source of high-energy neutrinos.

summary.plain: On 22 September 2017 IceCube detected a neutrino of about 290 TeV whose arrival direction was consistent with a known gamma-ray blazar, TXS 0506+056, that was observed to be in a flaring state. Telescopes from radio waves to gamma rays followed up, and the collaboration says the coincidence suggests that blazars may be a source of high-energy neutrinos.
summary.technical: The 290 TeV track alert IceCube-170922A was spatially coincident with the flaring gamma-ray blazar TXS 0506+056. A multiwavelength campaign across radio to VHE gamma rays characterised the flare, including the first VHE gamma-ray detection of the source.

title: Multi-messenger observations of a flaring blazar coincident with high-energy neutrino IceCube-170922A
why_it_matters: The abstract notes that individual astrophysical sources previously detected in neutrinos were limited to the Sun and the supernova 1987A, and that the origins of the diffuse flux of high-energy cosmic neutrinos remained unidentified; this neutrino-blazar coincidence "suggests that blazars may be a source of high-energy neutrinos".
